abstract: This paper develops the AI Occupational Exposure (AIOE) index, a systematic measure linking advances in AI capabilities to occupational task requirements using O*NET data. The methodology maps progress on specific AI benchmarks (e.g., image recognition, language understanding, translation) to the task composition of 800+ occupations, producing a continuous exposure score for each occupation. The key finding inverts common automation-risk intuitions: unlike previous waves of automation that primarily threatened low-skill, low-wage routine work, AI exposure is highest among high-skill, high-wage occupations. Occupations like market research analysts, financial managers, and clinical psychologists score high on AIOE, while occupations involving physical dexterity and manual tasks score low. The paper also examines industry and geographic variation in AI exposure, finding that metro areas with high concentrations of professional services and finance are most exposed. The AIOE index has become a foundational measure in the AI-and-labor literature, widely used by subsequent researchers and policymakers.
keyFindings: High-skill, high-wage occupations have the highest AI exposure, inverting the pattern from previous automation waves that primarily threatened low-skill routine work.
The AIOE index links specific AI capability benchmarks (image recognition, language understanding, translation) to O*NET occupational task requirements across 800+ occupations.
Occupations in professional services, finance, and information sectors face the greatest AI exposure, while occupations requiring physical dexterity and manual labor face less exposure.
Geographic exposure varies by metro area: regions with high concentrations of professional and financial services face greater aggregate AI exposure than manufacturing-heavy regions.
The AIOE measure has become a standard index in the AI-and-labor literature, used by the Federal Reserve, Census Bureau, and academic researchers to classify occupational AI risk.
methodology: The AIOE index is constructed by mapping AI capability benchmarks from the Electronic Frontier Foundation's AI Progress Measurement project to O*NET occupational ability requirements. Each occupation receives a weighted exposure score based on how much its task requirements overlap with abilities where AI has demonstrated rapid progress. Published in Strategic Management Journal. Data cover US occupations classified by O*NET.
qualifiers: The AIOE index measures exposure (overlap between AI capabilities and occupational tasks) rather than actual automation or displacement risk. High exposure does not necessarily mean high displacement if AI augments rather than replaces workers. The index is based on pre-generative-AI benchmarks and may not fully capture LLM-era capabilities. The mapping from AI benchmarks to occupational abilities requires subjective judgment at several steps. The index does not account for organizational, regulatory, or social barriers to AI adoption.
